hardening.minimized_reason: Build MariaDB without PAM: no auth_pam plugins, no setuid-root auth_pam_tool, and nothing that loads libpam.
hardening.pledge_reason: No package-enforced pledge-style capability policy is claimed; the Werewolf mariadb forms leash mariadbd.

changes.what: MariaDB's newest stable release, the highest-versioned GitHub release that is not a prerelease, as one unversioned package set: mariadb, mariadb-client, mariadb-dump and the rest.
changes.why: Wolfi keeps one recipe for MariaDB's newest series and renames it each quarter, release candidates included (13.0.1, then 13.1.1). Forms need one name that moves only to stable releases; mariadb-init upgrades the data when it does.

changes.what: Build with PLUGIN_AUTH_PAM=NO and PLUGIN_AUTH_PAM_V1=NO, and drop linux-pam-dev.
changes.why: The PAM plugins brought libpam and the setuid-root auth_pam_tool. Werewolf's MariaDB authenticates local users by unix_socket and others by password, never through PAM.

changes.what: Drop the OCI entrypoint subpackage with its pwgen dependency, and the self-provides and virtual-package tests that an unversioned name makes redundant.
changes.why: Werewolf leashes mariadbd as a service rather than running Wolfi's container entrypoint, and the aliases now name the real packages.

wolfi.removal_condition: Wolfi tracks MariaDB's stable releases under stable package names and builds without PAM; review compatibility before retiring this context.
